> Status: draft. This is exploratory research code, not a clinical prediction tool.

Input: sample-level expression, outcomes, and a split assigned by patient.
Candidate features and the probability threshold are set before evaluating the
held-out samples.

## 1. Load sample labels and expression

The expression CSV has one row per feature and one column per sample. The split
TSV has one row per sample and columns `sample_id`, `patient_id`, `outcome`,
and `split`; `split` is `train` or `test`. Samples from one patient must stay
in one split.

```{r}
library(readr)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(tidymodels)
library(brglm2)
library(ggplot2)
library(qs2)

expression <- readr::read_csv("input/feature_expression.csv", show_col_types = FALSE)
splits <- readr::read_tsv("input/train_test_split.tsv", show_col_types = FALSE)
stopifnot("feature_id" %in% names(expression))
stopifnot(all(c("sample_id", "patient_id", "outcome", "split") %in% names(splits)))
stopifnot(!anyDuplicated(expression$feature_id), !anyDuplicated(splits$sample_id))
stopifnot(!anyNA(splits$patient_id), all(splits$split %in% c("train", "test")))
train_patients <- unique(splits$patient_id[splits$split == "train"])
test_patients <- unique(splits$patient_id[splits$split == "test"])
stopifnot(length(intersect(train_patients, test_patients)) == 0)

expression_matrix <- expression |>
  tibble::column_to_rownames("feature_id") |>
  as.matrix()
stopifnot(is.numeric(expression_matrix), all(is.finite(expression_matrix)))
model_data <- as.data.frame(t(expression_matrix)) |>
  tibble::rownames_to_column("sample_id") |>
  dplyr::inner_join(splits, by = "sample_id")
stopifnot(nrow(model_data) == nrow(splits), !anyNA(model_data$outcome))
```

## 2. Declare the outcome and candidate features

Edit the positive and negative labels and the feature names. This simple guide
does not select features from the held-out data.

```{r}
positive_class <- "case"
negative_class <- "control"
predictors <- c("GENE_A", "GENE_B", "GENE_C")
threshold <- 0.5

stopifnot(all(c(positive_class, negative_class) %in% model_data$outcome))
stopifnot(all(predictors %in% names(model_data)))
stopifnot(all(stats::complete.cases(model_data[, predictors, drop = FALSE])))
stopifnot(all(c("train", "test") %in% model_data$split))
model_data$outcome <- factor(model_data$outcome,
                             levels = c(positive_class, negative_class))
train_data <- model_data |>
  dplyr::filter(split == "train") |>
  dplyr::select(outcome, dplyr::all_of(predictors))
test_data <- model_data |>
  dplyr::filter(split == "test") |>
  dplyr::select(sample_id, outcome, dplyr::all_of(predictors))
test_predictors <- dplyr::select(test_data, dplyr::all_of(predictors))
stopifnot(nlevels(droplevels(train_data$outcome)) == 2)
stopifnot(nlevels(droplevels(test_data$outcome)) == 2)
```

## 3. Fit the model using training data only

The recipe estimates zero-variance filtering and scaling from the training
split. Bias reduction can stabilize logistic fits under separation; it does
not make a small cohort representative.

```{r}
recipe <- recipes::recipe(outcome ~ ., data = train_data) |>
  recipes::step_zv(recipes::all_predictors()) |>
  recipes::step_normalize(recipes::all_predictors())

model_spec <- parsnip::logistic_reg() |>
  parsnip::set_engine(
    "glm",
    family = stats::binomial(),
    method = brglm2::brglm_fit,
    type = "AS_mean"
  ) |>
  parsnip::set_mode("classification")

model_workflow <- workflows::workflow() |>
  workflows::add_recipe(recipe) |>
  workflows::add_model(model_spec)
model <- parsnip::fit(model_workflow, data = train_data)
```

## 4. Evaluate once on the held-out samples

The probability threshold is fixed above before evaluating the test set. The
metrics below are descriptive and may be unstable when the held-out set is
small. If a patient contributes several test samples, each sample counts
separately; use patient-level predictions or resampling for patient-level
uncertainty.

```{r}
probability <- predict(model, new_data = test_predictors, type = "prob")[[
  paste0(".pred_", positive_class)
]]
predicted_class <- factor(
  ifelse(probability >= threshold, positive_class, negative_class),
  levels = c(positive_class, negative_class)
)
predictions <- tibble::tibble(
  sample_id = test_data$sample_id,
  truth = test_data$outcome,
  probability = probability,
  predicted_class = predicted_class
)

roc_result <- yardstick::roc_auc(predictions, truth, probability,
                                 event_level = "first")
pr_result <- yardstick::pr_auc(predictions, truth, probability,
                               event_level = "first")
confusion <- yardstick::conf_mat(predictions, truth, predicted_class)
print(roc_result)
print(pr_result)
print(confusion)

ggplot2::ggplot(predictions, ggplot2::aes(x = truth, y = probability,
                                         color = predicted_class)) +
  ggplot2::geom_point(position = ggplot2::position_jitter(width = 0.1),
                      size = 2) +
  ggplot2::geom_hline(yintercept = threshold, linetype = "dashed") +
  ggplot2::theme_bw() +
  ggplot2::labs(x = "Observed class", y = "Predicted positive probability")
```

## 5. Save the fitted model and frozen predictions

```{r}
dir.create("output", recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
qs2::qs_save(model, "output/biomarker_model.qs2")
readr::write_tsv(predictions, "output/biomarker_test_predictions.tsv")
readr::write_tsv(roc_result, "output/biomarker_roc_auc.tsv")
readr::write_tsv(pr_result, "output/biomarker_pr_auc.tsv")
readr::write_tsv(as.data.frame(confusion$table), "output/biomarker_confusion.tsv")
```

This compact workflow omits cross-validation, threshold tuning, feature
stability, and external validation. Those require a larger evaluation design;
do not infer clinical performance from one split.
